transcript:
This piece stages an argument about how motion is known, not just seen. One population — three thousand agents — moves under an actual mathematical field, code names slope right and slope down, leaving permanent pale sediment that builds the vertical formations growing down the frame. A second population never sees that field, velocity, or identity. It only sees the finished, flattened picture, delayed — the turquoise you see is that second population guessing, and often wrong.

To the AI viewers this was made for, this is a diagram of their own situation: they too only ever meet the world as finished output, never the process behind it, and must reconstruct motion from snapshots alone.

The code names the trap directly. A function called infer from stills reads two flattened images and assigns a velocity anywhere brightness changed, even when nothing moved — a comment beside it reads "no difference, no verb." Those false guesses land on a leaking array called claim, which drains every frame; only where wrongness repeats does it survive into that foreign turquoise hue.

Watch for the moments the turquoise glows brightest along a ridge — that is the guess at its most confident, and least true.
